# dsh-git-branch

> npm package: **`dsh-git-branch-plugin`** (`npm i dsh-git-branch-plugin` /
> `dsh plugin add dsh-gi

t-branch-plugin`). The GitHub repository is
> MYiYang/dsh-git-branch; the
> in-plugin id `dsh-git-br

anch`, the route prefix `/git-branch/api` and the
> loader row id `git-branch` are unaffected by the

route prefix `/git-branch/api` and the
> loader row id `git-branch` are unaffected by the npm name.

A DSH Web plugin that puts the current Git branch into the session composer,
lists every local and r

emote branch there, lets you switch local branches, and
opens a read-only commit graph.

- **Visible only for Git projects.** The chip is hidden when the session's
working directory is not

inside a Git repository.
- **Where:** the compact control row of the message composer
(`conversation

.input.left`), left of the model selector.
- **What it shows:** the current branch name; on a detach

ed HEAD it shows
`HEAD@<short commit>`.
- **Branch table:** click the chip to open a four-column tab

HEAD it shows
`HEAD@<short commit>`.
- **Branch table:** click the chip to open a four-column table:
| Column | Local branch | Remote branch |

| Branch | name (check mark when checked out) | name (globe) |
| Upstream | tracking ref, e.g. `orig

in/main` | *empty* |
| Ahead·Behind | `↑2 ↓1` vs. upstream, `=` when in sync | *empty* |
| Last comm
it | short hash (subject/date in the tooltip) | short hash |

Local rows are grouped first, then remote rows. A search field appears for
repositories with more th

an 8 branches and filters both groups. Switching
(`git checkout <branch>`) is offered for local bran

ches only — remote rows are
display-only, so clicking one never detaches HEAD or creates a branch.
F

ailures (dirty tree conflicts, invalid state) are shown inside the menu.
- **Commit graph:** the but

ton in the menu header opens a read-only graph panel
(above the chip when there is room, otherwise b

elow). It draws lanes and dots
[该节后续省略]
## Layout
| File | Role |
| `index.js` | Host half: mounts the trust-fenced `POST /git-branch/api/{status,checkout,graph}` rou

te and resolves the session's working directory. |
| `git.js` | The git layer: argv-only git invocat
ions, local/remote branch listing (upstream, ahead/behind, last commit), branch switch, commit-graph

read, detached-HEAD and non-repository detection. |
| `graph.js` | Pure commit-log parser and `git
log --graph`-style lane layout used by the graph panel — no repository or DOM access, fully unit-tes

ted. |
| `client.js` | Web client half: the composer chip, the four-column branch table, the commit-

graph panel, polling, and locale wiring. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch inserting the Host ro

w (`git-branch`). |
| `locale/*.json` | Plugin Manager title/description (English and Chinese). |
|

`icon.svg` | Plugin icon. |
| `test/git.test.js` | Git-layer tests over throwaway repositories (incl

uding a real remote). |
| `test/graph.test.js` | Parser/layout unit tests plus a real merge-history

smoke test. |
| `test/route.test.js` | Route tests through the real `apply` and handler. |
## How the halves talk
The browser cannot run git, so the Client half calls the one Host route:

- `status` → `{ isRepo, root?, branch?, detached?, commit?, branches }` for the
session's live worki

ng directory (`workingDirectory.get(session)`, falling
back to the session header's `cwd`). Each bra

mote rows carry only `name` and `lastCommit`, and the Client leaves the
upstream / ahead-behind cell

s empty for them.
- `checkout` → `git checkout <branch>` there (local names only), then the same
sta

tus shape.
- `graph` → `{ root, rows }` where each row is a commit plus its lane geometry:
`{ hash,

short, parents, author, time, subject, refs, head, lane, nodeColor,
nodeFromTop, links: [{ from, to,

color }], laneCount }`. A link runs from a
lane at the top edge (`from`), the commit's dot (`null`,

for a parent) or to a
lane at the bottom edge (`to`, for this commit's parents).

The route is registered through `ctx.webServer` and fenced with
`ctx.connection.requestRejection`, s

o only the authenticated Harness page can
call it; it accepts `POST` only. The directory never comes

from the request, and
a branch name is checked against the repository's own `refs/heads` listing
be
fore checkout, so a request cannot reach an arbitrary path or a git flag.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package is a DSH **bundle** (it ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`), so adding
it installs the dep

endency and activates the Host row. Make sure the package is
also listed in the profile's `dsh.profi

le.bundles` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`);
without that entry the bundle is installed but nev

(`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`);
without that entry the bundle is installed but never layered.

After installing or editing this package, restart DSH so the Host half loads the
new route, then ref

resh the Harness page so the browser loads the current
`client.js` (an open page can keep the client
module it already loaded).
## Test
From this directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

or `npm test`. The suite builds throwaway repositories under the OS temp
directory and removes them

afterwards; one fixture also creates a bare remote
to exercise remote-tracking refs, `origin/HEAD` a
nd ahead/behind counts.
## Notes and limits

- Switches **local** branches only; remote branches are listed read-only
(checking one out would det

ach HEAD or need a new local branch — both are
terminal/agent actions).
- The commit graph is read-o

nly and caps at the most recent 200 commits across
all refs. It never runs `git log` with a path or

revision taken from the
request; the repository is always the session's own.
- Uses `git checkout` r

ather than `git switch` so it also works on the Git 2.18
shipped with some Windows hosts.
- The plug

in resolves git once — the `subprocess` service's execution world
first, then a PATH scan — and PROB

ES every candidate with `git --version`.
A non-executable PATH shim (for example a Windows `git.bat`

no git can start, the chip simply stays hidden.
- The working directory is re-resolved on every req

uest, so a session that moved
into a linked worktree shows that worktree's branch.
